paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes a training-free inference-time framework for multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning, combining entropy-based route selection with step-wise attention-level visual enhancement.
dominant_domain: Multimodal reasoning, multimodal chain-of-thought, selective thinking, visual attention enhancement, training-free inference.
must_cover: The paper defines low-quality multimodal reasoning as both overthinking on easy questions and insufficient visual use on hard questions.
Selective Thinking estimates question difficulty from the entropy of the first generated answer token and chooses direct answering or chain-of-thought reasoning.
Step-wise Visual Enhancement amplifies attention on task-related visual patches during each reasoning step without inserting extra visual tokens.
Relative attention removes option-induced or edge-biased attention and produces more relevant visual focus.
Across eight benchmarks and four backbone settings, SDR-MCoT improves accuracy while using far fewer generated tokens than standard CoT.
key_numbers: Qwen2-VL-7B average accuracy: No CoT 59.00, CoT 57.34, MMCoT 61.75, SDR-MCoT 63.69.
Qwen2-VL-7B token consumption: No CoT 35.54, CoT 172.08, DDCoT 760.41, MMCoT 189.15, CCoT 920.35, ICoT 237.54, SDR-MCoT 67.94.
InternVL3-8B average accuracy: No CoT 70.28, CoT 65.90, MMCoT 70.89, SDR-MCoT 72.87.
LLaVA-1.5-7B average accuracy: No CoT 43.54, ICoT 44.37, SDR-MCoT 45.81.
LLaVA-1.5-13B average accuracy: No CoT 46.40, SDR-MCoT 48.57.
Ablation with Qwen2-VL-7B: no module tokens 212.91; Selective Thinking only tokens 74.07; both modules tokens 69.84.
Ablation accuracy on CoMT/MMStar/HallusionBench rises from 28.37/53.62/63.76 without modules to 32.39/56.39/69.12 with both modules.
The abstract reports more than 6% average accuracy improvement and about 60% token reduction over zero-shot CoT on Qwen2-VL-7B.
real_comparisons: Compared with No CoT, SDR-MCoT preserves direct answering for easy cases while enabling step-by-step reasoning for difficult cases.
Compared with standard CoT, SDR-MCoT avoids forcing every sample into a long reasoning trace.
Compared with ICoT and image-insertion methods, SDR-MCoT does not add extra visual tokens; it adjusts visual attention within decoding.
Compared with MMCoT, SDR-MCoT obtains stronger average results with substantially lower token cost in the reported Qwen2-VL setting.

central_claims.claim: The first-token entropy of a brief direct answer is a useful signal for deciding whether a multimodal question needs long reasoning.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The experiments and Figure 4 trend show that higher entropy correlates with lower accuracy on the sampled M3CoT groups, making entropy a practical route-selection proxy.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove that entropy is calibrated across all model families, prompts, languages, or open-ended answer spaces.

central_claims.claim: Visual enhancement can improve multimodal reasoning without inserting extra visual tokens.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The step-wise attention intervention improves reported accuracy and keeps generated-token cost low on the evaluated benchmarks.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not show the method works for architectures where attention maps or visual token internals are inaccessible.

central_claims.claim: Selective Thinking and Visual Enhancement are complementary.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Table 2 shows Selective Thinking mainly reduces token use, Visual Enhancement mainly improves accuracy, and their combination gives the best tradeoff.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not isolate every possible interaction between threshold choice, enhancement factor, and benchmark type.

claim_boundaries: The method is training-free for model parameters, but it still requires access to token logits and internal attention tensors.
The entropy threshold is adaptively estimated from a small subset, so deployment in a new distribution may require recalibration.
The method is evaluated on standard multimodal reasoning benchmarks; real interactive agent environments are not directly tested.
Visual enhancement changes attention weights after softmax and may depend on the model's attention implementation.
negative_or_limiting_results: Standard CoT can underperform No CoT on Qwen2-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B, showing that longer reasoning is not automatically useful.
Selective Thinking alone has limited accuracy gain; it mainly reduces token cost.
Visual Enhancement alone does not reduce token cost and slightly increases generated tokens in the ablation.
The paper does not provide an extensive limitation section; deployment risks must be inferred from the need for logits, attention maps, and threshold calibration.
mechanism_result_map: First-token entropy maps to the Selective Thinking route decision and the Figure 4 entropy-accuracy trend.
Relative attention maps to Figure 5, where option-aware and option-free attention are combined to reduce noise.
Morphological erosion maps to removing isolated attention-sink patches before visual token amplification.
Attention amplification maps to Table 2, where Visual Enhancement improves CoMT, MMStar, and HallusionBench accuracy.
comparative_positioning: SDR-MCoT is closest to ICoT and DaP-ICoT in goal, but it intervenes on attention rather than reinserting image crops.
It is complementary to VisRef: VisRef reinjects selected visual tokens, while SDR-MCoT amplifies selected visual attention without token growth.
It is complementary to PRCR: PRCR reduces the system cost of visual revisiting, while SDR-MCoT decides whether and how to reason in the first place.
It sits on the TrainingFree side of the Reasoning collection because it does not add SFT or RL.
reuse_takeaways: For 3D agent reasoning, use a cheap uncertainty signal before invoking long planning or multi-view evidence retrieval.
Separate route selection from evidence enhancement; one controls budget, the other controls grounding quality.
When using multiple-choice prompts, remove option-induced attention bias before deciding which visual evidence matters.
Report token consumption together with accuracy, because multimodal CoT methods can hide large inference costs.
followup_questions: Can first-token entropy be replaced by a calibrated verifier when answer spaces are long or open-ended?
Does attention amplification remain reliable under grouped-query attention, flash attention, or quantized inference kernels?
Can the relative-attention idea be extended to multi-view 3D render selection?
Would combining SDR-MCoT with PRCR or VisRef yield a stronger low-token visual revisiting pipeline?
